summary: The note describes the growth of outdoor experiential education in the post-pandemic world of 2023, led by figures such as Dr. Emily Forrest and Marcus Leong. It covers cognitive and emotional benefits, environmental stewardship, the balance between technology and nature, life skills, and community and inclusion. It concludes that policy and funding are shifting to support outdoor learning, with an optimistic outlook for the next decade.
one_line: Outdoor experiential learning is spreading, with research, tech tools and programs showing benefits for cognition, wellbeing, sustainability, life skills and inclusion.
key_facts: Educational experts gathered on September 4th, 2023 to contemplate the future of learning, with outdoor classrooms seen as an essential component of holistic education.
Dr. Emily Forrest led a seminar on September 15th presenting research on integrating outdoor experiences into the daily curriculum.
Marcus Leong founded the startup "GreenLearn" in fall 2023, which built an interactive platform that helps teachers create immersive outdoor lesson plans.

Researchers at the University of Natural Endeavors found that outdoor education students showed higher problem-solving skills, memory retention, and creativity; Prof. Jonathan Hales led the study and spoke on October 12th.
Dr. Sandra McKay's mental wellbeing study, presented on November 8th, found outdoor learning increased self-esteem, improved mood, and reduced anxiety.

Dr. Alan Chen, an ecologist and educational consultant, said on December 5th that connecting lessons to real-world ecological challenges empowers students to become proactive agents of sustainability.
Experts like Dr. Chen anticipated that by 2033 these experiences would produce a generation motivated to pursue sustainability.
Alicia Torres, a technology integration specialist, said on January 6th, 2024 that technology used mindfully can be an ally in the outdoor classroom, not a distraction.
"EcoQuest", an edu-gaming venture launched on February 20th, pioneered games that take students on virtual eco-adventures.
Jake Moreno, an outdoor educator, said on March 15th that rope courses and group hikes develop leadership, teamwork, and resilience.
The "Lead and Learn" program, established on April 5th, combines leadership theory with practical outdoor activities.
Sarah Gibson, a social psychologist and educator, launched the "Outdoor Bridges" initiative on May 2nd and called nature "a great equalizer".
Governments and private sectors began investing more in green spaces and in funding programs that support outdoor education.
